tasks.short: Follow the planned design to decide where to plant

steps.what: Find the planned landscaping designs for this bed
Read the designs for grass, flowers and foliage quantities
Walk the beds and match the planned landscaping designs
Determine where to plant flowers, foliage or sow grass

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store opens the named landscaping design for the bed. Where that design holds a plant schedule as a table, the quantities for grass, flowers and foliage sit on the same screen. The worker still walks the ground and still determines where to plant.
tasks.previous_blocker: The planned design is a paper set in the van or the site hut, so the worker hunts the sheet before walking the bed.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can open a named revision, and a plant schedule that is already a table can be shown beside it.
tasks.still_hard: The bed edge, the shade and the soil are only visible on the ground, and a plant in the wrong place is rework.
tasks.human_edge: Only the person on the bed can see whether the drawing's line matches the ground, the shade and the soil.
tasks.altitude: The worker still walks every bed and still decides where to plant. A named design is easier to find when it is filed. No new right to change the design.

reach.learn: Which planned designs the crew could not match to the ground.

evidence.claim: Matching a landscape drawing to a bed is still done by the person standing there. A list of plant quantities does not show the bed edge, the shade or the soil. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The design file holds a name, a revision and a site area. When a plant schedule exists it is a table of species, quantity and bed code. The producer is the landscape designer. A paper set stays a manual read inside the find step.
A drawing with no schedule table leaves the quantity list empty. The worker still reads the drawing on the ground, and that time stays in the walk and the determine steps.
The record stores the design name and revision. It does not store where the worker walked, and it does not score the worker.
Test the document store's own folder for the named revision before any custom code.
Laying the sod and planting are later tasks. This task ends when the worker has determined the places.
Upkeep is the half hour per 100 baseline hours to point a bed at the revision that is actually on site.
unknowns: Whether this employer's designs are filed by bed and revision, or only kept as paper on the van.
research_questions: Is the plant schedule a table in the design file, or only lettering on the drawing?

already_counted.description: Check the opened design is the revision named for this bed.
Check the noted quantities against the schedule rows before walking.

incremental.description: Point a bed at the revision that is on site when the link is wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most beds start from a paper drawing the supervisor unfolds on site, with no plant-schedule table, so the quantity list is empty and the worker still walks every bed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The grounds worker still walks the beds and still decides where to plant. A named design opens faster when it is filed. No new authority over the design.
reach: First-line supervisor of landscaping: which planned designs the crew could not match to the ground.
skills_to_grow: Match a design line to the bed edge.
Reject a quantity the plant schedule does not state.
role.ambitious_version: The named design opens before the walk, and a plant schedule that is a table shows the quantities. The worker still matches the drawing to the ground and still decides where to plant.
